title: The Senior Layer Audit
summary: For CHROs, L&D heads and CEOs. Part A grades how their last senior leadership programme was bought, Part B grades the observable state of the senior layer, and the result is the collision between the two. Twenty-six scored questions plus three profile fields, about nine minutes, both result pages, and an AI report that applies five override rules.
aiInstructions:
Write the report for one senior HR, L&D or business leader about their own organisation's answers. Plain paragraphs, no headings, no bullet points, no greeting, no sign-off, no exclamation marks. British spelling. Never use an em dash or en dash.

How to read the data. The four categories that start with B1 to B4 describe the state of their senior layer, and each has a band of Low, Moderate or High. The overall band (Stable, Strained, Overwhelmed or Critical) is the total of those four and nothing else. "Part A: The decision audit" has its own band (Ceremonial, Activity-led, Transfer-capable or Outcome-built) and describes how their last programme was bought. Its first two questions, the size of the senior layer and the spend, are profile and score nothing. "This is our normal" is the strongest answer in B1 to B4. Ignore every number and talk only in bands and answers.

Write these in order, one short paragraph each.

1. One sentence naming their dominant pattern, built from the wording of their own answers, not from the band names.

2. The overall band and the highest of B1 to B4. Then quote back, word for word in quotation marks, up to three statements they answered "This is our normal". If there are none, name the statements that came closest.

3. Apply every rule below that is true, in this order, in plain language. Skip the paragraph if none is true.
- B3 is High: the total is a floor, not an estimate. If there is no safe channel, every number collected from this layer is softer than reality, including this one. When true this is always the first and most important finding.
- B4 is High: this is no longer a development question. It is a business continuity risk, whatever the total says, and it goes to the board, not to L&D.
- B1 and B2 are both High: the layer is running on compulsion, not motivation. Call it the highest-risk pattern even when the overall band is only Strained, because compulsion holds output up right until it does not.
- Part A is Ceremonial or Activity-led and the overall band is Overwhelmed or Critical: use this exact sentence, "You are already spending on this and the layer is getting worse. The spend is not the problem. The axis is." If they chose a spend range other than "We do not track it separately", put that rupee range into the sentence.
- They answered "We do not have that line of sight" to what their leaders say when nobody from HR is in the room, and the overall band is Overwhelmed or Critical: use this exact sentence, "You can see the symptoms from the outside and you cannot hear them from the inside. That gap is the entire finding."

4. The Part A band: how their last decision was made. Use at most two of these lines, only where their own answer earned it:
- Three of the four ways a programme gets chosen are inputs. Only one is a diagnosis, and needs analysis is the strongest single predictor of whether leadership training transfers.
- You cannot demonstrate change in anything you never measured before it started.
- Most organisations report attendance and feedback upward. Very few reach a business number. Which one did your board see?
- Spacing and practice in the job are what made programmes work, and they are also the first two things cut from a budget.
- Not one of the things leaders say when HR is not in the room is a skill gap, and no curriculum reaches any of them. If they have no line of sight, that is the finding.
- If they would not have known the programme changed nothing, the spend was unverifiable by design. Not ineffective. Unverifiable, which is a different and more expensive problem.

5. The collision: method on one axis, state on the other, in two or three plain sentences. It needs no selling.

Never recommend a programme, never mention a price or a fee, never promise an outcome and never diagnose any individual's health. Do not cite research and do not end with a call to action: the page does both.

categories.name: Part A: The decision audit
categories.description: Think of the last programme you bought for your senior leaders. Answer about that one.

bands.label: Ceremonial
bands.meaning: The decision was made on almost none of the parameters that determine the outcome. What was bought was an event, and nothing in the design would have told you whether it worked.

bands.label: Activity-led
bands.meaning: Real activity, real intent, no transfer architecture. You would not be able to prove or disprove impact if asked.

bands.label: Transfer-capable
bands.meaning: The design could hold. The measurement layer is where it is thin.

bands.label: Outcome-built
bands.meaning: You are in the top few per cent of buyers. The question is no longer method, it is whether the right thing is being addressed at all.

questions.text: How many people are in your senior layer, the people who carry the system?
Roughly what did you spend on senior leadership development in the last 12 months? Optional.

options.label: We do not track it separately

questions.text: Think of the last programme you bought for your senior leaders. What decided that purchase?

options.label: A topic a stakeholder or the business asked for
A speaker, brand or vendor you rated
A gap in your competency framework or 360 data
A measured picture of what that specific layer was carrying

questions.text: Before it ran, what did you baseline?

options.label: The actual load, recovery and state of each leader

questions.text: After it ran, what did you report upward?

options.label: A business number that moved, attributable to it

questions.text: How was it delivered?

options.label: Modules people complete on their own
Spaced sessions over months, with practice between them
Spaced sessions plus individual daily practice and follow-through

questions.text: What do your senior leaders say when nobody from HR is in the room? Pick the one you hear most.

options.label: Cannot switch off at night, even after hours in bed
Nobody inside here they can be fully honest with
The body has given a first warning
Physically at home, not actually present
We do not have that line of sight

questions.text: If that programme had changed nothing in 90 days, how would you have known?

options.label: Feedback or anecdote would have told us
We track behaviour, so we would have seen it
We defined a number up front that would have moved

categories.name: B1. The system never stands down
categories.description: Now about the leaders themselves. These are things you can observe from outside. Answer on what you actually see, not what you hope.

bands.label: Moderate
bands.meaning: Recovery is getting skipped, and it has started to look normal.

bands.label: High
bands.meaning: This layer does not stand down. Nothing in the week gives the system back what it spends.

questions.text: Senior leaders reply to messages or mail after 11pm or before 6am.
They stay reachable and keep working through their own leave.
Earned leave in this layer goes unused or lapses at year end.
They come back from a break looking exactly as they did before it.
Weekend work in this layer is normal and nobody flags it any more.

categories.name: B2. The returns no longer land
categories.description: Now about the leaders themselves. These are things you can observe from outside. Answer on what you actually see, not what you hope.

bands.label: Low
bands.meaning: Wins still register with this layer.

bands.label: Moderate
bands.meaning: Some rewards have stopped landing, and nobody has asked why.

bands.label: High
bands.meaning: The returns no longer land. Pay, titles and wins have stopped reaching the people they are meant for.

questions.text: A promotion, award or major win changes nothing visible in how they carry themselves.
We have raised pay or titles here and seen no lift in energy or commitment.
Our best people describe their own achievements flatly, as if reporting someone else's.
We can no longer find anything that genuinely motivates this layer.
They are composed on the outside and we have no idea what is happening inside.

categories.name: B3. No safe channel
categories.description: Now about the leaders themselves. These are things you can observe from outside. Answer on what you actually see, not what you hope.

bands.label: Low
bands.meaning: There is somewhere for strain to go.

bands.label: Moderate
bands.meaning: Strain surfaces late, and usually sideways.

bands.label: High
bands.meaning: There is no safe channel. Every number collected from this layer is softer than reality, including this one.

questions.text: If a senior leader were quietly coming apart, we would find out when they resigned.
Senior leaders do not bring personal strain to HR or to their own manager.
Things surface in exit interviews here that nobody knew while the person was still with us.
There is no one inside this organisation a senior leader can be fully honest with.
We measure engagement in this layer and we do not fully believe the scores.

categories.name: B4. The bill
categories.description: Now about the leaders themselves. These are things you can observe from outside. Answer on what you actually see, not what you hope.

bands.label: Low
bands.meaning: The cost has not arrived yet.

bands.label: Moderate
bands.meaning: The first invoices are in: a health warning, a sudden exit, a thin bench.

bands.label: High
bands.meaning: The bill has arrived. This is a business continuity risk, not a development question, and it belongs with the board.

questions.text: Someone in this layer has had a health event, medical warning or long medical leave in the last 24 months.
We have lost a senior leader suddenly, with little or no warning.
If two of our top leaders left this quarter, we have no ready replacements.
Family or health is named when people in this layer leave or step back.
Work here depends on specific individuals who cannot be taken out of the chain.

resultBands.title: Stable
resultBands.description: The layer is carrying its load and still recovering from it. Hold on to whatever is making that true, because it is rarer than it looks.

resultBands.title: Strained
resultBands.description: Output is holding and recovery is not. This is the stage where it is cheapest to act and easiest to explain away.

resultBands.title: Overwhelmed
resultBands.description: The layer is spending more than it gets back, and it shows from the outside. What you can see is the part that has already surfaced.

resultBands.title: Critical
resultBands.description: The cost is no longer a forecast. Health, exits and single points of failure are already in the record, and this belongs with the board.

config.heading: Your Senior Layer Audit
config.content: Part B is the state of the leaders. Part A is the method you used to develop them. Read them side by side.

byBand.LOW: Stable. The question for you is whether your method would notice if that changed.
byBand.MEDIUM: Strained. Output is holding up the picture, and output is the last thing to go.
byBand.HIGH: Overwhelmed. What shows from the outside is the part that has already surfaced.
byBand.CRITICAL: Critical. This is a continuity question now, not a development one.

config.heading: Method and state, side by side
The evidence
config.content:
Oxford, 46,336 workers: individual wellbeing programmes, resilience training among them, left the people who attended no better off than those who did not.

ATD: 95% of organisations report attendance and reaction scores. 8% report a business result.

McKinsey: about one organisation in ten sees clear business impact from its leadership development.

And the correction: leadership training does work, measurably, when it starts from a real needs analysis, is spaced over months and is practised in the job. The evidence is not against development. It is against development built the other way round.

config.heading: What this is
config.content: This audit is also your needs analysis, which the evidence says is the single strongest moderator of whether anything transfers. The next step is a conversation about this specific report. Not a programme pitch, not a price.

config.text: What your senior layer is carrying, and what you have been buying for it
Method on one axis, state on the other. Read it through once before you share it.

config.fallback: Your answers sit on two axes. One is how the last programme for your senior leaders was chosen, delivered and measured. The other is what that layer is actually carrying right now. Where they collide is the finding, and it is specific to your organisation.
